title: Telemetry deprecation & migration sprint plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint-level plan and companion notes for deprecating legacy telemetry collectors and migrating to a unified OTEL + Prometheus/Grafana stack in private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Focus: minimize customer disruption, preserve alert fidelity, and migrate Terraform-managed resources with minimal drift.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: OTEL collector replacement for existing fluentd/rsyslog pipelines, Prometheus upgrade (2.x -> 2.47) and remote_write to internal long-term storage (S3-compatible), Grafana upgrade and dashboard migration, Terraform module tweaks, RBAC/networking changes in VPC and on-prem kube clusters.
- Out of scope: hosted API telemetry changes, customer-managed non-Redwood agents.

Assumptions:
- Customers have private control planes with a cluster-admin contact and at least one maintenance window available.
- K8s versions >=1.24 for most private deployments; flag any cluster <1.20 as special case.
- Existing TF modules for observability live under infra/telemetry and will be versioned (semver) before migration.

Goals/KPIs for the migration sprint:
- Zero critical alerts lost during migration (verify via replay).
- Less than 2% increase in token-latency SLO violations attributable to telemetry changes in the first 7 days post-migration.
- TF drift < 1 file per cluster and automated fix PRs created for any drift detected.

High-level approach:
1) Prepare: inventory current telemetry footprint per customer (prom targets, scrape intervals, logging agents, retention).
2) Stage: deploy OTEL collector + receiver sidecar in a staging cluster; configure remote_write to a staging S3 bucket; deploy demo Grafana with migrated dashboards.
3) Pilot: pick 2 customers (one VPC, one on-prem baremetal) for a canary migration during their maintenance window.
4) Iterate: collect regressions, tune scrape configs, adjust resource requests/limits.
5) Rollout: automated TF upgrade across remaining clusters with policy for automatic rollback on threshold breach.

Terraform module notes (developer-facing):
- Module layout: infra/telemetry/ (prometheus/, grafana/, otel/). Each submodule exposes inputs: cluster_id, kubeconfig_secret, s3_remote_write_bucket, retention_days, scrape_interval_seconds, resource_profile (small|medium|large), enable_node_exporter (bool).
- Backwards-compat: add new optional variables rather than replacing existing names. Introduce prometheus_version variable defaulting to current stable.
- State migration: move prometheus helm_release resource into prom submodule; use terraform state mv with scripted checks. Document command sequence in ops-runbook.
- Outputs: grafana_admin_secret, prom_endpoint, otel_collector_configmap_hash (used by rollout guard).
- Testing: add a smoke-test resource that creates a synthetic metric and validates scrape via remote_write (using a small test harness).

Prometheus/Grafana upgrade plan (detailed):
- Pre-upgrade checks:
  - Confirm rule files validate with promtool check-rules.
  - Run promcheck against existing rules to surface deprecated functions.
  - Validate record rule cardinality estimates (avoid explosion after upgrade).
  - Snapshot current TSDB backups (wal and block snapshot) and upload to S3-compatible archive.
- Upgrade steps (canary cluster):
  - Scale down Thanos/remote-write consumers to drain traffic.
  - Upgrade helm chart + prometheus image.
  - Run promtool check-config on the live config.
  - Reconcile alertmanager routes if needed.
- Post-upgrade validation:
  - Compare alert firing counts for the first 2 hours vs previous baseline.
  - Verify remote_write success rate > 99.5% for 24h.
  - Verify rule evaluation time distribution (p95) unchanged or improved.
- Rollback plan:
  - Use helm rollback or terraform state rollback steps; if TSDB is incompatible, restore snapshot and restart previous chart image.

OTEL collector migration notes (specifics):
- Replace legacy fluentd -> splunk/http pipelines with a unified otel-collector configured with receivers: prometheus, filelog, fluentforward (if necessary). Use processors: batch, attributes, resource/attribute mapping, memory_limiter. Exporters: prometheus_remote_write, otlp/HTTP (to internal inference pipeline), aws_s3 (for logs in S3-compatible object store).
- Resource sizing heuristics (per collector):
  - small (dev/test): 0.25 CPU, 512Mi RAM, 10mbps egress
  - medium (prod low-throughput): 1 CPU, 2Gi RAM, 50mbps egress
  - large (high-throughput): 2-4 CPU, 8-16Gi RAM, 200mbps+ egress
- Deployment model options (pick one per customer):
  - Daemonset collector (node-local) with tailing receivers for logs; good for low-latency metrics and node metrics.
  - Centralized collectors (deployment) behind service with fluentforward receiver from agents; good for resource-constrained nodes.
- Config drift mitigation: compute configmap hash and store as TF output; if hash changes unexpectedly, block automated rollouts and create PR for human review.

Log shipping & retention strategy:
- Logs: structured JSON preferred. Use OTEL processor to normalize fields (timestamp, trace_id, span_id, service.name, severity, message).
- Ship to: primary S3-compatible long-term store (encrypted), and short-term hot store (internal ELK equivalent for 7 days).
- Retention policy: default 30 days hot, 365 days cold (customer-configurable).
- Compression: gzip for objects, use object lifecycle rules to transition to cheaper classes.

Pre-migration checklist (operator friendly):
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and SA contact.
- [ ] Export current prometheus rule snapshots and grafana dashboards JSON.
- [ ] Generate TF plan and save planfile to artifact store.
- [ ] Run smoke tests against staging remote_write.
- [ ] Validate RBAC: TF will need permissions: create/patch deployments, configmaps, secrets, serviceaccounts, clusterroles (where applicable).

Migration execution steps (operator):
1) Create feature branch in infra repo and bump module version.
2) Run terraform plan with -target for prom submodule in canary cluster.
3) Apply and monitor prom and otel collector for 15 minutes.
4) Run synthetic metrics test and logging replay for 60 minutes.
5) If green, expand to cohort of 5 clusters via CI run (parallel where network permits).

Post-migration verification (automated):
- Alert fidelity comparison report (auto-generated): count of alerts matching by name and labels over last 24h pre/post.
- Scrape success rate by job > 99.9% (alert if < 99%).
- Remote_write error rate < 0.5% sustained.
- Dashboard health: screenshots diff for top 20 dashboards (automated with grafana-screenshot tool).

Rollback triggers (auto + manual):
- Auto: >3 customer-critical alerts triggered that are not present pre-migration; remote_write success < 95% for 30m; CPU memory > 90% for 10m on collectors.
- Manual: customer reports missing traces/logs for a service; unexpected rule explosions.

Operator runbook snippets (copyable):
- TF state move example:
  terraform state mv module.telemetry.module.prometheus.helm_release.prom release.module.prometheus.helm_release.prom
- Prom tool config check:
  promtool check-config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
- Grafana backup dashboards (curl):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAFANA_ADMIN" "https://$GRAFANA/api/dashboards/uid/$UID" -o $UID.json

Open/known questions:
- How to best replay logs for alert validation without exposing PII? (suggestion: anonymize pipeline using otel attributes processor).
- Does the customer's offline air-gapped cluster have a pattern for transferring TSDB snapshots? We need documented SFTP/USB workflow.
- Should we support both node-local daemonset and centralized collectors for the same cluster during migration? Risk: duplicate metrics.

Timeline & owners (proposed 6-week sprint):
- Week 0: Inventory + module prep (owner: Priya)
- Week 1-2: Staging deployments + config validation (owner: Diego)
- Week 3: Canary migrations (owner: Hannah)
- Week 4: Wider cohort rollout (owner: Priya)
- Week 5: Final rollouts, cleanup TF deprecations (owner: Diego)
- Week 6: Post-mortem and documentation handoff (owner: Hannah)

Appendix: sample terraform variables (text, paste into module variables.tf)
- variable "prometheus_version" { type = string default = "2.47.0" description = "Prometheus server image tag" }
- variable "otel_collector_profile" { type = string default = "medium" description = "resource sizing profile for oc-collector" }
- sample terraform apply (canary):
  export TF_WORKSPACE=customer-canary
  terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan-canary.tfplan -var="cluster_id=cust-1234" && terraform apply "plan-canary.tfplan"

Notes to self / next steps (informal):
- Need to add prometheus recording rules audit to the release checklist so we don't accidentally introduce high-card rules.
- Build grafana screenshot pipeline into CI for dashboard drift detection.
- Add an otel collector config lint check in CI to block invalid processors.

End of draft.
